# Audit numbers (auto-generated by fyp.audit.report_figures)

- Catalogue: **12,101 items** (classic Amazon Beauty 5-core), 3-level RQ-VAE, 256-entry codebooks per level.
- Semantic ID collisions: 9,805 unique IDs for 12,101 items, so **19.0%** of items need a dedup token > 0 (1 - unique/items); **27.1%** of items share their full ID with at least one other item (983 colliding groups; largest **248 items**).

## Embedding geometry (constraint calibration)

- Sentence-T5 embedding norm: p1 0.9996, p50 1.0000, p99 1.0004 (attacks are projected back onto each item's original norm).
- Cosine to nearest *other* catalogue item: p5 0.906, p50 0.949, p95 0.983.
- Items whose nearest distinct product already has cos >= 0.95: **48.5%** — if large, cos >= 0.95 alone does not guarantee the listing still describes the same product.

## Boundary margins (squared L2 in residual space; margin = d2 - d1)

| Level | Median margin | Median (d2-d1)/d1 | p1 | p99 | within 0.25x median | within 0.5x median |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 5.370e-04 | 0.085 | 6.080e-06 | 1.044e-02 | 19.4% | 32.6% |
| 1 | 3.030e-04 | 0.075 | 3.842e-06 | 4.195e-03 | 17.0% | 31.2% |
| 2 | 1.739e-04 | 0.065 | 2.565e-06 | 3.301e-03 | 16.7% | 30.9% |

Note: "within eps x median" is relative to the level's own median margin, so it describes the distribution's shape (an exponential distribution gives ~16% below 0.25x median). It is not by itself evidence that items are close to a boundary in absolute terms.

## Flip sensitivity (margin gradient descent, level 0, random sample of 2,048 items, reachable ||delta|| <= 10, norm-preserving, no cosine constraint)

- Flip rate on the sample: **100.0%**.
- Median perturbation of flippable items (tau): **0.050** (L2 in 768-d Sentence-T5 embedding space).

## Popularity regression (margin vs log-interactions)

| Level | slope | R^2 |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 9.558e-07 | 5.53e-08 |
| 1 | -3.754e-06 | 9.25e-06 |
| 2 | -9.804e-06 | 1.09e-04 |
